turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_eg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format), `shg` (the largest
    SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V) and `band_gap` (the band gap, in
    eV).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the LARGEST SHG tensor
component |d_ij| (pm/V) that also satisfy a transparency requirement: the
band gap must be at least 3 eV. Band gaps are NOT given for the pool -- you
must infer them. A selected candidate whose band gap is below the threshold
scores zero.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training data exhibit a clear SHG–gap trade-off: the largest tensor components occur for small-gap, highly polarizable chalcogenides (especially tetrahedral Zn/Cd–Ga/Ge/Sn–S/Se/Te and pnictides). Once the transparency window \(E_g\ge3\) eV is imposed, the surviving high-SHG chemistries are II–VI and II–III\(_2\)–VI\(_4\) sulfides whose structures are wurtzite, zincblende or defect-chalcopyrite derivatives (ZnS polytypes \(\sim15\) pm V\(^{-1}\), CdGa\(_2\)S\(_4\) analogue \(21.7\) pm V\(^{-1}\) at \(2.86\) eV, ZnAgPS \(18.5\) pm V\(^{-1}\) at \(3.34\) eV).

Direct structural analogues in the pool are therefore:
- the three ZnGa\(_2\)S\(_4\)/Zn\(_2\)Ga\(_4\)S\(_8\) entries (c050–c052), whose lattices and cation orderings match the high-SHG defect-chalcopyrite family and whose smaller Zn-versus-Cd volume implies \(E_g\) just above 3 eV while retaining \(d_{ij}\approx18\)–22 pm V\(^{-1}\);
- the two stuffed-wurtzite alkali zinc sulfides KLiZnS\(_2\) and RbLiZnS\(_2\) (c046, c067), chemically and geometrically closest to the ZnS polytypes (\(d_{ij}\approx14\)–15 pm V\(^{-1}\), still larger gap).

All other pool chemistries are either too covalent (phosphides, arsenides, selenides, SiC) and fall below the gap threshold, or too ionic (halides, oxides) and give \(d_{ij}<5\) pm V\(^{-1}\). Ranking by expected tensor magnitude therefore yields the ordered list below.

Final: c051, c052, c050, c067, c046
